title: Enterprise region admissions checklist & prioritization matrix
creator: Leah Morgan
description:
Purpose: Create a repeatable, auditable checklist and scoring matrix for admitting enterprise customer requests that affect region availability, data residency, and failover topology. This ticket captures the intake fields, scoring weights, required artifacts, decision gates, and handoffs between PM/Legal/Infra/Support.

Scope: New region requests, residency constraints (data at rest vs. sovereignty), active-active failover requests, and exceptions for contractual residency. Does NOT include low-risk self-serve region preferences for hosted tiers.

Why: We've seen inconsistent decisioning across account teams, ad-hoc infra work duplication, and slow time-to-yes for enterprise contracts. The deliverable will reduce time-to-decision, improve cost forecasting, and surface security/compliance blockers earlier.

Artifacts & links: Confluence intake template (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GEO/Residency+Intake+Draft; Intake form prototype (Google Forms): https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1Example; Initial cost model (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleCosts; Related PM doc: PM-6247.

Owner & Next steps: PM owns rubric and checklist (this ticket). Infra owns feasibility assessment template. Legal provides required data-handling statements. Support owns customer comms template. After adoption, loop to Solutions Eng for field enablement.
triage_matrix:
Scoring weights (total 100): business-criticality 30, regulatory+legal risk 25, implementation complexity (infra + ops) 20, revenue impact (annualized) 15, latency/residency user impact 10. Decision bands: 80+ approve for Dedicated/Private roadmap, 60-79 approve with staged pilot/contract clause, <60 requires exec review.

Implementation complexity scale: 1 (no infra changes, config-only) to 5 (new region + KMS + on-prem changes). Legal risk flags: data sovereignty law, export controls, contractual restrictions.

Minimum required intake fields: customer name, contract value (ARR), regulatory requirements, data class, desired region(s), required failover SLA, timeline, justification, tech contacts, Security/Compliance contact, existing Redwood product usage, preferred deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A completed intake checklist template in Confluence covering all required fields and URLs to artifacts.
2) A numeric prioritization matrix implemented in a shared spreadsheet that auto-calculates band and recommended route (hosted/dedicated/private).
3) A one-page decision playbook for SDR/AE/SE with clear next-step actions per decision band.
4) Legal and Infra sign-off on sample 3 enterprise requests using the matrix.
5) Handoff doc & triage rota created in Support and Solutions Engineering.
6) Pilot: apply to next 2 incoming residency requests and capture time-to-decision metric (target < 10 business days).
communication_plan:
Stakeholders: PM (Leah Morgan), Infra Lead (Marcos Nguyen), Legal (Priya Rao), Solutions Eng (Diego Alvarez), Support Manager (Karen Liu), Sales Ops.
Channels: #geo-onboarding Slack channel for real-time questions, confluence page for canonical docs, weekly 30-min sync during pilot.
Customer comms: templated intake acknowledgement within 24 hours, estimated SLA for final decision published to customer within 10 business days for pilot.
Escalation: if matrix score <60 or legal risk identified, route to Head of Product + Head of Legal for decision within 5 business days.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (this ticket): finalize rubric and checklist + legal/infrastructure approval. Phase 1 (pilot): apply to 2 live enterprise requests, collect feedback, measure time-to-decision and rework rate. Phase 2: publish to GTM and embed intake into sales onboarding flow. Phase 3: instrument in Console and automate initial feasibility checks (future ticket).
